obligations.statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorised person always confirms that the product licence and approval requirements are met for that batch.
obligations.quote: The authorised person responsible for approving a batch for release shall always ensure that the following requirements have been met:- (a) the licence and the approval requirements for the product have been met for the batch concerned

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that the GMP principles and guidelines of this Part were followed.
obligations.quote: the principles and guidelines of GMP, as laid down in this Part, have been followed

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that the main manufacturing and testing processes are validated.
obligations.quote: the principal manufacturing and testing processes have been validated

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that all needed checks and tests were done and that production conditions and manufacturing records were taken into account.
obligations.quote: all the necessary checks and tests have been performed and account taken of the production conditions and manufacturing records

obligations.statement: Before any product is released, the authorised person confirms that planned changes or deviations in manufacturing or QC were reported through a well-defined reporting system; such changes may also need notifying to, and approval by, the licensing authority.
obligations.quote: any planned changes or deviations in manufacturing or QC have been notified in accordance with a well-defined reporting system before any product is released. Such changes may need notification and approval by the licensing authority

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that any extra sampling, inspection, tests and checks needed to cover planned changes and deviations were done or started, as appropriate.
obligations.quote: any additional sampling, inspection, tests and checks have been carried out or initiated, as appropriate, to cover planned changes and deviations

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that all needed production and QC documents are complete and signed off by supervisors trained in the relevant disciplines.
obligations.quote: all necessary production and QC documentation has been completed and endorsed by supervisors trained in appropriate disciplines

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that appropriate audits, self-inspections and spot-checks are done by experienced, trained staff.
obligations.quote: appropriate audits, self-inspections and spot-checks are carried out by experienced and trained staff

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that the head of quality control has given approval.
obligations.quote: approval has been given by the head of quality control

obligations.statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that all relevant factors were considered, including those tied to the specific output batch under review (such as sub-division of output batches from a common input, or continuous production runs).
obligations.quote: all relevant factors have been considered, including the factor associated with the output batch directly under review (e.g., sub-division of output batches from a common input, factors associated with continuous production runs)

obligations.statement: Where useful, data may also be recorded by means other than the computerised system, alongside it.
obligations.quote: Data may be recorded by other means in addition to the computer system.

obligations.statement: The licensee has prepared a concise Site Master File giving specific, factual GMP information on the production and/or control of the pharmaceutical preparations made at the licensed premises.
obligations.quote: The licensee shall prepare a succinct document in the form of ‘Site Master File’ containing specific and factual Good Manufacturing Practices about the production or control or both of pharmaceutical manufacturing preparations carried out at the licensed premises.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers general information: a short profile of the firm, the manufacturing activities permitted by the licensing authority, any other activities on the premises, licensed product types with process flow charts, staff numbers in production, QC, storage and distribution, any outside scientific, analytical or technical help, products registered in foreign countries, and short descriptions of the quality management system, pharmaceutical quality system and quality risk assessment.
obligations.quote: General information:- (a) brief information of the firm; (b) pharmaceutical manufacturing activities as permitted by the licensing authority; (c) other manufacturing activities, if any, carried out in the premises; (d) type of products licensed for manufacture with flow charts mentioning procedure and process flow; (e) number of employees engaged in the production, quality control, storage and distribution; (f) use of outside scientific, analytical or other technical assistance in relation to manufacture and analysis; (g) products details registered with foreign countries. (h) short description of the Quality Management System of the firm; (i) pharmaceutical Quality System; and (j) quality risk assessment.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers personnel: an organisation chart showing QA, production and QC arrangements, key personnel qualifications, experience and responsibilities, an outline of basic and in-service training and how training records are kept, health requirements for production staff, and hygiene and clothing requirements.
obligations.quote: Personnel:- (a) organisational chart showing the arrangement for quality assurance including production and quality control; (b) qualifications, experience and responsibilities of key personnel; (c) outline for arrangements for basic and in-service training and how the records are maintained; (d) health requirements for personnel engaged in production; and (e) personnel hygiene requirements, including clothing.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers premises: a scale plan or description of manufacturing areas, the nature of construction and fixtures or fittings, and a short description of the ventilation systems.
obligations.quote: Premises:- (a) simple plan or description of manufacturing areas drawn to scale; (b) nature of construction and fixtures or fittings; (c) brief description of ventilation systems.

obligations.statement: In the Site Master File, ventilation is described in more detail (with schematic drawings of the systems) for critical areas with a potential risk of airborne contamination.
obligations.quote: More details shall be given for critical areas with potential risk of airborne contamination (schematic drawing of systems).

obligations.statement: The Site Master File states the classification of the rooms used to manufacture sterile products.
obligations.quote: Classification of the rooms used for the manufacture of sterile products shall be mentioned

obligations.statement: The Site Master File also covers special areas for handling highly toxic, hazardous and sensitising materials, a short description of the water system with schematic drawings and its sanitation, and the planned preventive maintenance programme for premises with its recording system.
obligations.quote: special areas for the handling of the highly toxic, hazardous and sensitising materials; (e) brief description of water system (schematic drawings of systems), including sanitation; and (f) description of planned preventive maintenance programmes for premises and of the recording system.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers equipment: a short description and list of major production and QC laboratory equipment, the planned preventive maintenance programme for equipment with its recording system, and qualification and calibration, including recording systems and the arrangements for validating computerised systems.
obligations.quote: Equipment:- (a) brief description of major equipment used in production and Quality Control Laboratories (a list of equipment required); (b) description of planned preventive maintenance programmes for equipment and of the recording system; and (c) qualification and calibration including the recording systems and arrangements for computerised systems validation.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers sanitation by showing that written specifications and procedures exist for cleaning manufacturing areas and equipment.
obligations.quote: Sanitation:-availability of written specifications and procedures for cleaning manufacturing areas and equipment.

obligations.quote: Documentation:- (a) arrangements for the preparation, revision and distribution of; (b) necessary documentation for the manufacture; and (c) any other documentation related to product quality that is not mentioned elsewhere (e.g., microbiological controls about air and water).

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers production: a short description of production operations, using flow sheets and charts with important parameters wherever possible, how starting materials, packaging materials, bulk and finished products are handled (including sampling, quarantine, release and storage), how rejected materials and products are handled, and the general process validation policy.
obligations.quote: Production:- (a) brief description of production operations using, wherever possible, flow sheets and charts specifying important parameters; (b)arrangements for the handling of starting materials, packaging materials, bulk and finished products, including sampling, quarantine, release and storage; (c) arrangements for the handling of rejected materials and products; and (d)brief description of general policy for process validation.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers quality assurance and control: the documentation system, change control, the master validation plan and validation policy, product quality review, a description of the QC system and QC department activities, and the procedures for releasing finished products.
obligations.quote: Quality Assurance and Control:- (a) documentation system; (b) change control; (c) master validation plan and validation policy; (d) product quality review; and (e) description of the quality control system and of the activities of the QC Department. Procedures for the release of the finished products.

obligations.statement: For manufacture under loan licence, the Site Master File describes how the loan licensee's GMP compliance is assessed.
obligations.quote: Manufacture under loan licence and licensee:- description of the way in which compliance of GMP by the loan licensee shall be assessed.

obligations.quote: Distribution, complaints and product recall:- (a) arrangements and recording system for distribution; and (b)arrangements for the handling of complaints and product recalls.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File gives a short description of the self-inspection system, stating whether an outside, independent, experienced expert took part in evaluating GMP compliance across all aspects of production.
obligations.quote: Self-inspection:- short description of the self-inspection system indicating whether an outside, independent and experienced external expert was involved in evaluating the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production.

obligations.statement: The Site Master File covers export: the products exported to each country and any related complaints and product recalls.
obligations.quote: Export of drugs:- (a) products exported to different countries; and (b) complaints and product recall, if any.

obligations.statement: The quality system achieves product realisation by designing, planning, implementing, maintaining and continually improving a system that consistently delivers products with the right quality attributes.
obligations.quote: A Pharmaceutical Quality System appropriate for the manufacture of medicinal products should ensure that: (i) Product realisation is achieved by designing, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes

obligations.statement: Product and process knowledge is managed across every lifecycle stage.
obligations.quote: Product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages

obligations.statement: Medicinal products are designed and developed taking GMP requirements into account.
obligations.quote: Medicinal products are designed and developed in a way that takes account of the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practice

obligations.statement: Production and control operations are clearly defined and GMP is applied.
obligations.quote: Production and control operations are clearly specified and Good Manufacturing Practice adopted

obligations.statement: Management responsibilities are clearly defined.
obligations.quote: Managerial responsibilities are clearly specified

obligations.statement: Arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for choosing and monitoring suppliers, and for verifying that each delivery comes from the approved supply chain.
obligations.quote: Arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is from the approved supply chain

obligations.statement: Processes exist to manage outsourced activities.
obligations.quote: Processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities

obligations.statement: A state of control is set up and kept by building and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.
obligations.quote: A state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality

obligations.statement: Product and process monitoring results are used in batch release, in deviation investigations, and to take preventive action against future deviations.
obligations.quote: The results of product and processes monitoring are taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations, and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future

obligations.statement: All necessary controls on intermediate products, other in-process controls and validations are performed.
obligations.quote: All necessary controls on intermediate products, and any other in-process controls and validations are carried out

obligations.statement: Continual improvement is supported by putting in place quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.
obligations.quote: Continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge

obligations.statement: Planned changes are evaluated in advance and approved before implementation, taking account of regulatory notification and approval where required.
obligations.quote: Arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation of planned changes and their approval prior to implementation taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required

obligations.statement: After any change is implemented, an evaluation confirms the quality objectives were met and product quality was not harmed unintentionally.
obligations.quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended deleterious impact on product quality

obligations.statement: A suitable level of root cause analysis is applied when investigating deviations, suspected product defects and other problems; the level can be set using quality risk management principles.
obligations.quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis should be applied during the investigation of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems. This can be determined using Quality Risk Management principles.

obligations.statement: Where the true root cause cannot be found, the most likely root cause(s) are identified and addressed.
obligations.quote: In cases where the true root cause(s) of the issue cannot be determined, consideration should be given to identifying the most likely root cause(s) and to addressing those.

obligations.statement: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this is justified after making sure that process, procedural or system errors or problems, if present, were not overlooked.
obligations.quote: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this should be justified having taken care to ensure that process, procedural or system based errors or problems have not been overlooked, if present.

obligations.statement: Appropriate corrective and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) are identified and taken in response to investigations.
obligations.quote: Appropriate corrective actions and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) should be identified and taken in response to investigations.

obligations.statement: The effectiveness of CAPAs is monitored and assessed in line with quality risk management principles.
obligations.quote: The effectiveness of such actions should be monitored and assessed, in line with Quality Risk Management principles

obligations.statement: Medicinal products are not sold or supplied until an Authorised Person has certified that each production batch was made and controlled in line with the Marketing Authorisation and other relevant regulations on production, control and release.
obligations.quote: Medicinal products are not sold or supplied before an Authorised Person has certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of medicinal products

obligations.statement: Satisfactory arrangements ensure, as far as possible, that products are stored, distributed and later handled so their quality is kept throughout shelf life.
obligations.quote: Satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the medicinal products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf life

obligations.statement: A self-inspection and/or quality audit process regularly appraises how effective and applicable the pharmaceutical quality system is.
obligations.quote: There is a process for self-inspection and/or quality audit, which regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the Pharmaceutical Quality System

obligations.statement: The manufacturer, and the Marketing Authorisation holder where different, evaluate the product quality review results and assess, under the quality system, whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed.
obligations.quote: The manufacturer and, where different, Marketing Authorisation holder should evaluate the results of the review and an assessment made as to whether corrective and preventive action or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the Pharmaceutical Quality System.

obligations.statement: Management procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of the resulting actions, and their effectiveness is verified during self-inspection.
obligations.quote: There should be management procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions and the effectiveness of these procedures verified during self-inspection.

obligations.statement: Where scientifically justified, quality reviews may be grouped by product type (for example solid, liquid or sterile products).
obligations.quote: Quality reviews may be PE 009-18 (Part I) -6- 24 September 2026 Chapter 1 Pharmaceutical Quality System grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, sterile products, etc. where scientifically justified.

obligations.statement: Where the Marketing Authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement sets out each party's responsibilities for producing the product quality review.
obligations.quote: Where the Marketing Authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, there should be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the product quality review.

obligations.statement: The Authorised Person responsible for final batch certification and the Marketing Authorisation holder ensure the quality review is done on time and is accurate.
obligations.quote: The Authorised Person responsible for final batch certification together with the Marketing Authorisation holder should ensure that the quality review is performed in a timely manner and is accurate.

Such actions may include the issuance of cautionary communications to healthcare professionals in relation to their use of a batch that is potentially defective.

obligations.statement: Such risk-reducing actions are considered case by case and discussed with the competent authorities concerned.
obligations.quote: These should be considered on a case-by-case basis and discussed with the concerned Competent Authorities.

obligations.statement: The data governance system ensures data lifecycle controls proportionate to quality risk management principles.
obligations.quote: The data governance system should ensure controls over the data lifecycle which are commensurate with the principles of quality risk management.

obligations.statement: Data lifecycle controls may include organisational measures (procedures for completing and retaining records, staff training and documented authorisation for generating and approving data, governance system design that controls risks across how data is generated, recorded, processed, retained and used, routine data verification such as daily, batch- or activity-related checks, periodic surveillance such as self-inspection, and staff with data integrity and security expertise) and technical measures (computerised system validation, qualification and control, automation, or technologies giving greater data control).
obligations.quote: These controls may be:  Organisational o procedures, e.g. instructions for completion of records and retention of completed records; o training of staff and documented authorisation for data generation and approval; o data governance system design, considering how data is generated, recorded, processed, retained and used, and risks or vulnerabilities are controlled effectively; o routine (e.g. daily, batch- or activity-related) data verification; o periodic surveillance, e.g. self-inspection processes seek to verify the effectiveness of the data governance system; or o the use of personnel with expertise in data management and integrity, including expertise in data security measures.  Technical o computerised system validation, qualification and control; o automation; or o the use of technologies that provide greater controls for data management and integrity.

obligations.statement: The effectiveness of data integrity controls is assessed periodically through self-inspection (internal audit) or other periodic reviews, to confirm that data lifecycle controls work as intended.
obligations.quote: The effectiveness of data integrity control measures should be assessed periodically as part of self-inspection (internal audit) or other periodic review processes. This should ensure that controls over the data lifecycle are operating as intended.

obligations.statement: Beyond routine data verification checks (such as daily, batch- or activity-related checks), self-inspections include a wider review of controls, including a check that staff still understand good data management for patient protection and that the working environment stays quality-focused with open reporting of issues (for example by reviewing ongoing data management training).
obligations.quote: In addition to routine data verification checks (e.g. daily, batch- or activity- related), self-inspection activities should be extended to a wider review of control measures, including:  A check of continued personnel understanding of good data management practice in the context of protecting of the patient, and ensuring the maintenance of a working environment which is focussed on quality and open reporting of issues (e.g. by review of continued training in good data management principles and expectations).

obligations.statement: Self-inspections include a review of reported data and outcomes against raw entries, which may cover data not checked routinely (where risk-justified) and/or a sample of already-verified data to confirm the routine process still works.
obligations.quote: A review for consistency of reported data/outcomes against raw entries. This may review data not included during the routine data verification checks (where justified based on risk), and/or a sample of previously verified data to ensure the continued effectiveness of the routine process.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections include a risk-based sample of computerised system logs and audit trails to confirm GMP/GDP-relevant information is reported accurately, particularly where routine system data is reviewed manually or through a validated exception report.
obligations.quote: A risk-based sample of computerised system logs / audit trails to ensure that information of relevance to GMP/GDP activity is reported accurately. This is relevant to situations where routine computerised system data is reviewed manually or by a validated ‘exception report’

obligations.statement: Self-inspections include a review of quality system metrics (trending) that may also indicate how effective data governance is.
obligations.quote: A review of quality system metrics (i.e. trending) that may also be indicators of data governance effectiveness.

obligations.statement: The pharmaceutical quality system can prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in systems or processes that could lead to data integrity lapses.
obligations.quote: The company’s Pharmaceutical Quality System should be able to prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in the system or their processes that may lead to data integrity lapses.

obligations.statement: The company knows its data lifecycle and builds in suitable controls and procedures so that generated data are valid, complete and reliable.
obligations.quote: The company should know their data life cycle and integrate the appropriate controls and procedures such that the data generated will be valid, complete and reliable.

obligations.statement: Control and procedural changes for data integrity may address areas such as quality risk management, investigations, data review practices, computerised system validation, IT infrastructure, services and security, vendor and contractor management, training on data governance, handling of completed records (including cloud storage), oversight of purchasing critical equipment and IT with data integrity requirements, self-inspection covering data quality and integrity, and quality metrics reported to senior management.
obligations.quote: Specifically, such control and procedural changes may be in the following areas:  Quality Risk Management,  Investigation programs,  Data review practices (section 9),  Computerised system validation,  IT infrastructure, services and security (physical and virtual),  Vendor/contractor management,  Training program to include company’s approach to data governance and data governance SOPs,  Storage, processing, transfer and retrieval of completed records, including decentralised/cloud-based data storage, processing and transfer activities,  Appropriate oversight of the purchase of GMP/GDP critical equipment and IT infrastructure that incorporate requirements designed to meet data integrity expectations, e.g. User Requirement Specifications, (Refer section 9.2)  Self-inspection program to include data quality and integrity, and  Performance indicators (quality metrics) and reporting to senior management.

obligations.statement: Where summary data are shared between sites of the same organisation, the supplying site's compliance may be evaluated by alternative means, such as evidence of following corporate procedures or internal audit reports.
obligations.quote: Where summary data is distributed between different sites of the same organisation, the evaluation of the supplying site’s compliance may be determined through alternative means (e.g. evidence of compliance with corporate procedures, internal audit reports, etc.).

obligations.statement: The quality unit sets up a programme and schedule for ongoing audit trail reviews, based on each system's criticality and complexity, to verify current controls work and to detect potential non-compliance.
obligations.quote: The company’s quality unit should establish a program and schedule to conduct ongoing reviews of audit trails based upon their criticality and the system’s complexity in order to verify the effective implementation of current controls and to detect potential non-compliance issues.

obligations.statement: Audit trail reviews are built into the company's self-inspection programme.
obligations.quote: These reviews should be incorporated into the company’s self-inspection programme.

obligations.statement: Procedures exist to address and investigate audit trail discrepancies, including escalation to senior management and national authorities where necessary.
obligations.quote: Procedures should be in place to address and investigate any audit trail discrepancies, including escalation processes for the notification of senior management and national authorities where necessary.

obligations.statement: Audit trail reviews include both random selections and targeted selections based on criticality or risk.
obligations.quote: Audit trail reviews should be both random (selected based on chance) and targeted (selected based on criticality or risk).

obligations.quote: These elements will vary depending on the source, the supply chain and the subsequent use of the excipient, but as a minimum the following high level GMP elements should be considered by the manufacturing authorisation holder: (a) establishment and implementation of an effective pharmaceutical quality system

obligations.statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there is a supplier qualification programme.

obligations.statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether systems ensure every contracted-out activity is covered by a written contract.

obligations.statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether an effective system is maintained for reviewing complaints and recalling excipients.

obligations.statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there is a change management and deviation management system.
obligations.quote: change management and deviation management system

obligations.statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there is a self-inspection programme.
obligations.quote: self-inspection program

obligations.statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether environmental controls and storage conditions are in place.

obligations.statement: The distributor carries out and records self-inspections to monitor implementation of and compliance with these GDP guidelines.
obligations.quote: The distributor should conduct and record self-inspections in order to monitor the implementation of and compliance with these guidelines.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections are carried out regularly to an approved schedule.
obligations.quote: Regular self-inspections should be performed in accordance with an approved schedule.

obligations.statement: Procedures exist for safely removing waste, including toxic chemical and biological waste, reagents, samples, solvents and air filters.
obligations.quote: Procedures should be in place for the safe removal of types of waste including toxic waste (chemical and biological), reagents, samples, solvents and air filters.

obligations.statement: Antimicrobial waste from laboratory testing, though usually negligible next to manufacturing waste, is still considered in exceptional cases, such as when a QC laboratory tests very large sample quantities.
obligations.quote: The amount of antimicrobial waste being generated by laboratory testing activities is generally considered to be negligible compared to the amounts that are being generated by manufacturing activities but should still be considered in exceptional cases, e.g. if very large amounts of sample are being tested by a quality control laboratory.

obligations.statement: API and finished product manufacturers consider keeping a risk assessment of all contaminants from antimicrobial manufacturing if released into the environment, including the risk of resistant microorganisms developing.
obligations.quote: manufacturers of APIs and FPPs should consider retaining documentation on the following: ■■ a risk assessment for all contaminants related to antimicrobial manufacturing, in the event that they are released into the environment, and the associated risk of development of resistant microorganisms

obligations.statement: Based on that risk assessment, manufacturers consider keeping a waste-stream analysis for each antimicrobial produced, at API and finished product sites.
obligations.quote: based on the above risk assessment, waste-stream analysis for each antimicrobial agent produced (at API sites and FPP sites).

obligations.statement: The waste-stream analysis is repeated whenever a production change affects waste streams.

obligations.statement: Manufacturers consider keeping records of the quantity and nature of waste generated, including analytical data, documented analyses and findings on levels of antimicrobials or their precursors.
obligations.quote: the quantity and nature of the waste generated, including the analytical data and documentation of analyses performed and their findings on the levels of antimicrobial agents or their precursors

obligations.statement: Manufacturers consider keeping regular reports on collecting, treating and disposing of waste and wastewater, at a risk-based frequency consistent with applicable local, regional or international regulatory requirements.
obligations.quote: regular reports on the collection, treatment and disposal of waste and wastewater; the frequency should be risk-based and in line with local, regional or international regulatory requirements, as applicable

obligations.statement: The waste treatment methods are documented as effective for each specific antimicrobial or antimicrobial precursor.
obligations.quote: information on the methods used to treat the waste should be documented to be effective for each specific antimicrobial or antimicrobial precursor.

obligations.statement: Analytical data showing conversion of these substances and residues to non-hazardous waste are available at the facility and kept current.

obligations.statement: If effective treatment is not yet in place for all waste streams from each API or finished product, a documented time-limited strategy with specified milestones sets out actions towards treatment that significantly reduces the antimicrobial or precursor concentration (and its microbial source, when relevant).
obligations.quote: if effective waste treatment is not yet implemented for all waste streams resulting from the manufacture of each API or FPP, documentation on a time-limited strategy should be in place, with specified milestones for that implementation, specifying actions towards achieving treatment that significantly reduces the concentration of the antimicrobial substance or its precursor (and its microbial source, when relevant)

obligations.statement: Manufacturers consider keeping a rationale and risk assessment for their chosen decontamination methods for antimicrobial-containing manufacturing waste and/or their mitigation strategy.

obligations.statement: Incineration may be considered for solid or semi-liquid waste.

obligations.statement: A zero-liquid effluent or zero-discharge approach is adopted, especially where the risk is assessed as high or unclear.
obligations.quote: The zero-liquid effluent approach or zero-discharge policy is encouraged, especially when the risk is assessed to be high or unclear, as it prevents any contamination of the environment.

obligations.statement: The effectiveness and by-products of a treatment approach are considered when choosing it.

obligations.statement: This waste documentation is kept at the manufacturing facility even when an external contractor is used.

obligations.statement: Manufacturers use these points to consider in their self-audits to verify continued GMP compliance.

obligations.quote: there are systems for managing returns, complaints and recalls

obligations.statement: Systems exist for managing changes, deviations and CAPAs.
obligations.quote: there are systems to manage changes, deviations and corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs)

obligations.statement: The quality system includes self-inspections.
obligations.quote: The quality system should include self-inspections.

obligations.statement: Self-inspections monitor implementation of, compliance with and effectiveness of SOPs, and compliance with regulations, GSP, GDP and other relevant guidelines.
obligations.quote: These should be conducted to monitor the implementation, compliance with and effectiveness of SOPs, as well as compliance with regulations, GSP, GDP and other appropriate guidelines.

obligations.quote: Necessary CAPAs should be taken

obligations.statement: CAPA effectiveness is reviewed within a defined timeframe.

obligations.statement: Users audit and self-inspect their water systems at regular intervals.
obligations.quote: Users should conduct audits and self-inspection of water systems at regular intervals.

obligations.statement: Records of water system audits and self-inspections are kept.
obligations.quote: Records should be maintained.

obligations.statement: Data governance control strategies based on quality risk management principles are in place to prevent or mitigate risks.
obligations.quote: Data governance control strategies using quality risk management (QRM) principles (5) are required to prevent or mitigate risks.

obligations.statement: The control strategy aims to put in place appropriate technical, organisational and procedural controls.
obligations.quote: The control strategy should aim to implement appropriate technical, organizational and procedural controls.

obligations.statement: Controls may include procedures supporting data integrity compliance, a quality culture that encourages transparent reporting of failures with investigation and follow-up, controls that remove or reduce data risks to an acceptable level across the data life cycle, enough time and resources for a data integrity programme, monitoring through audits and self-inspections and continuous improvement, qualified and trained staff with regular GxP and data integrity training, validated computerised systems with the controls needed to protect electronic data, and defined roles and responsibilities for contract givers and acceptors in quality agreements and contracts with a focus on data integrity.
obligations.quote: Examples of controls may include, but are not limited to: ■■ the establishment and implementation of procedures that will facilitate compliance with data integrity requirements and expectations; ■■ the adoption of a quality culture within the company that encourages personnel to be transparent about failures, which includes a reporting mechanism inclusive of investigation and follow-up processes; ■■ the implementation of appropriate controls to eliminate or reduce risks to an acceptable level throughout the life cycle of the data; ■■ ensuring sufficient time and resources are available to implement and complete a data integrity programme; to monitor compliance with data integrity policies, procedures and processes through e.g. audits and self-inspections; and to facilitate continuous improvement of both; ■■ the assignment of qualified and trained personnel and provision of regular training for personnel in, for example, GxP, and the principles of data integrity in computerized systems and manual/ paper based systems; ■■ the implementation and validation of computerized systems appropriate for their intended use, including all relevant data integrity requirements in order to ensure that the computerized system has the necessary controls to protect the electronic data (3); and ■■ the definition and management of the appropriate roles and responsibilities for contract givers and contract acceptors, entered into quality agreements and contracts including a focus on data integrity requirements.

obligations.statement: A system exists for regularly reviewing data for consistency with ALCOA+ principles, covering paper and electronic records in daily work and in system and facility audits and self-inspections.
obligations.quote: There should be a system for the regular review of data for consistency with ALCOA+ principles. This includes paper records and electronic records in day-to-day work, system and facility audits and self-inspections.

obligations.statement: The effectiveness of implemented controls is evaluated, for example by tracking and trending data, reviewing data, metadata and audit trails (in areas such as warehouse and materials management, production, QC, case report forms and data processing), and routine audits and/or self-inspections that cover data integrity and computerised systems.
obligations.quote: The effectiveness of the controls implemented should be evaluated through, for example: ■■ the tracking and trending of data; ■■ a review of data, metadata and audit trails (e.g. in warehouse and material management, production, quality control, case report forms and data processing); and ■■ routine audits and/or self-inspections, including data integrity and computerized systems.

obligations.quote: retain records as evidence of the implementation of the audit programme and the audit results

obligations.statement: The laboratory has a director (or equivalent head) with a relevant university degree and supervisory experience in pharmaceutical analysis in a QC laboratory, regulatory body or industry, who holds full responsibility for all analytical, organisational, administrative and educational operations.
obligations.quote: The laboratory should have the following managerial and technical personnel: ■■ A laboratory director (or manager or head of the laboratory, or an appropriate job title) with appropriate qualiﬁcations (university degree in an appropriate discipline) for the position, with experience in a supervisory role in pharmaceutical analysis in a quality control laboratory, in the regulatory sector or in industry, who assumes full responsibility for all operations, including analytical, organizational, administrative and educational.

obligations.statement: The laboratory director ensures staff have competencies and qualifications suited to their functions and that their grades match their responsibilities.
obligations.quote: This person is also responsible for ensuring that: –– members of the laboratory staff have the competencies and qualifications appropriate to their required functions and their grades reﬂect their responsibilities

obligations.statement: The laboratory director ensures that the adequacy of existing staff training procedures is reviewed periodically.
obligations.quote: the adequacy of existing training procedures for staff is reviewed periodically

obligations.statement: The laboratory director ensures that technical management is adequately supervised.
obligations.quote: the technical management is adequately supervised

obligations.statement: The laboratory director ensures that certificates of analysis, analytical test reports and other important reports and protocols are approved.
obligations.quote: the certiﬁcates of analysis, analytical test reports and other important reports and protocols are approved

obligations.statement: The laboratory director is supported, preferably, by one or more technical managers or senior analysts with extensive QC pharmaceutical analysis experience who are designated responsible for analytical operations and for directly managing and supervising analysts and technicians.
obligations.quote: The laboratory director should preferably be supported and complemented by one or more technical managers (or senior analysts) with extensive experience in pharmaceutical analysis in a quality control laboratory, who have been designated responsibility for the analytical operations and for direct management and supervision of the team of analysts and technicians.

obligations.statement: The laboratory has a quality manager with the responsibility and authority to implement the QMS and quality control activities and ensure compliance with them.
obligations.quote: A quality manager who shall have the responsibility and authority to implement and ensure compliance with the QMS and quality control activities.

obligations.statement: Depending on laboratory size, the quality manager stays independent of routine analytical work.
obligations.quote: The quality manager should remain independent of routine laboratory analytical activities, depending on the size of the laboratory.

obligations.statement: The quality manager organises internal audits of laboratory activities, preferably with a staff member from another section, to a schedule approved at management review.
obligations.quote: The quality manager organizes internal audits of various laboratory activities, with the participation, preferably, of another member of staff from another section, according to a schedule approved during the management review.

obligations.statement: The quality manager, supported by technical managers as needed, ensures that staff operating specific equipment, instruments or devices are competent for those tasks.
obligations.quote: The quality manager, with the support of technical managers whenever necessary, ensures that: –– personnel operating speciﬁc equipment, instruments or other devices are competent for the tasks they are performing

obligations.statement: The quality manager ensures that staff doing tests, calibrations, validations or verifications are competent for those tasks.
obligations.quote: personnel involved in tests or calibrations, validations or veriﬁcations are competent for the tasks they are performing

obligations.statement: The quality manager ensures regular in-service training is arranged to update and extend the skills of analysts and technicians.
obligations.quote: regular in-service training programmes are arranged to update and extend the skills of both analysts and technicians

obligations.statement: The quality manager ensures the laboratory takes part regularly in suitable proficiency testing schemes and, where possible and applicable, collaborative studies.
obligations.quote: the laboratory participates regularly in suitable proﬁciency testing schemes and, whenever possible, collaborative studies (as applicable)

obligations.statement: The quality manager ensures due arrangements for safekeeping and control of poisons and narcotic, psychotropic and radioactive substances, which are kept locked up and handled and used only in designated places under an authorised person's supervision.
obligations.quote: due arrangements are made for the safekeeping and control of substances that are subject to poison regulation or to the controls applied to narcotic, psychotropic and radioactive substances, and which should be stored under lock and key, and handled and used in designated places under the supervision of an authorized person

obligations.statement: The laboratory has qualified analysts, normally graduates in pharmacy, analytical chemistry or another relevant subject, with the knowledge, skills and ability to perform their assigned tasks.
obligations.quote: Qualified analysts, who normally should be graduates in pharmacy, analytical chemistry or other relevant subject, with the requisite knowledge, skills and ability to adequately perform the tasks assigned to them by managers or supervisors.

obligations.statement: Suitably qualified, experienced analysts with a thorough grasp of the management system (including reviewing, interpreting and reporting results, the internal chain of custody, and CAPAs for analytical problems) are available to act as laboratory supervisors.
obligations.quote: Appropriately qualified and experienced analysts with a thorough understanding of the management system, including the review, interpretation and reporting of test results, the maintenance of an internal chain of custody, and proper implementation of corrective and preventive actions in response to analytical problems, should also be available to serve as laboratory supervisors.

obligations.statement: Technicians hold diplomas in their subjects from technical or vocational schools, or have the hands-on experience needed for their assigned activities.
obligations.quote: Technicians should hold diplomas in their subjects awarded by technical or vocational schools or have the requisite hands-on experience to perform the assigned activities.

obligations.statement: The laboratory has an appropriate staff training schedule, especially for staff who meet its technical and managerial needs.
obligations.quote: The laboratory should have an appropriate training schedule for staff, particularly for those staff who respond to the technical and managerial needs of the laboratory.

obligations.statement: Inputs to the training plan may be drawn from internal audits, management reviews, risk and opportunity assessments or other available sources.
obligations.quote: Inputs to the training plan can be gathered from internal audits, management reviews, risk and opportunity assessments, or other available options.

obligations.statement: After training is completed successfully, evaluation results are recorded and made available, and the competency matrix or master list is updated.
obligations.quote: On successful completion of training, the results of evaluation should be recorded and made available, and the information should be added to the competency matrix or master list.

obligations.statement: The QMS ensures sufficient resources, such as equipment, personnel and materials.
obligations.quote: The quality management system should ensure that: ■ sufficient resources are available (for example, equipment, personnel, materials)

obligations.statement: Excipients for pharmaceutical use are produced, controlled, stored and distributed in line with this guidance and associated guidelines, such as good QC laboratory practices and good storage and distribution practices, where appropriate.
obligations.quote: excipients for pharmaceutical use are produced, controlled, stored and distributed in accordance with the recommendations in this document and other associated guidelines, such as good quality control laboratory practices and good storage and distribution practices, where appropriate

obligations.statement: Managerial roles, responsibilities and authorities are clearly set out in job descriptions.
obligations.quote: managerial roles, responsibilities and authorities are clearly specified in job descriptions

obligations.statement: Operations and other activities are clearly described in writing, for example SOPs and work instructions.
obligations.quote: operations and other activities are clearly described in a written form, such as standard operating procedures and work instructions

obligations.statement: Appropriate arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct containers and labels.
obligations.quote: appropriate arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct containers and labels

obligations.statement: All necessary controls are in place.
obligations.quote: all necessary controls are in place

obligations.statement: Calibrations, verifications or validations are done where necessary.
obligations.quote: calibrations, verification or validations are carried out where necessary

obligations.statement: The excipient is processed and checked correctly against defined procedures and specifications.
obligations.quote: the excipient for pharmaceutical use is correctly processed and checked according to the defined procedures and specifications

obligations.statement: Deviations, suspected product defects, OOS results and other nonconformances or incidents are reported, investigated and recorded.
obligations.quote: deviations, suspected product defects, out-of-specification test results and any other nonconformances or incidents are reported, investigated and recorded

obligations.statement: A suitable level of root cause analysis is applied in these investigations and the most likely root causes are identified.
obligations.quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations and the most likely root causes are identified

obligations.statement: Proposed changes are evaluated and approved before implementation.
obligations.quote: proposed changes are evaluated and approved prior to implementation

obligations.statement: After a change that could affect quality or the product is implemented, an evaluation confirms the quality objectives were met and there was no unintended adverse effect on product quality.
obligations.quote: After implementation of a change that could impact the quality or the product, an evaluation should be undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality

obligations.statement: Appropriate corrective and preventive actions, and checks of their effectiveness where appropriate, are identified and taken.
obligations.quote: appropriate corrective actions and preventive actions, as well as checks on the effectiveness of those actions (where appropriate), are identified and taken

obligations.statement: Where required, processes exist to manage outsourced activities that could affect product quality, purity and integrity.
obligations.quote: where required, processes are in place to ensure the management of any outsourced activities that may impact product quality, purity and integrity

obligations.statement: No excipient batch is released and supplied until the quality unit has released it, assured that it was produced and controlled in line with product specifications, this guidance and other relevant regulations on production, control and release.
obligations.quote: a batch of an excipient for pharmaceutical use is not released and supplied before it has been released by the quality unit with the assurance that the batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with product specifications, and with the recommendations in this document and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of these products

obligations.statement: A system exists for handling complaints, returns and recalls.
obligations.quote: there is a system for handling complaints, returns and recalls

obligations.statement: A self-inspection system exists.
obligations.quote: there is a system for self-inspection

obligations.statement: A product quality review system exists.
obligations.quote: there is a system for product quality review
